title: Measure caption lines with real Inter Bold advances, not a 0.56 em average
body:
## Summary
The caption safe-zone check (captionSafeZoneViolations -> estimateLineWidth) sized lines as chars x 0.56 em, so upper-case lines that overflow the 837 px inner box were counted as fitting, and the publish gate's safe_zone_violations deny saw 0.

## Description
packages/captions/src/geometry.ts:52 estimated `line.length * AVG_CHAR_EM * fontSize`. Real Inter Bold sets upper case at ~0.65 em: 'MAXIMUM WORLD TITLE' (19 chars) is 935 px against 837 px, while the estimate said 809 px. The check feeds apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:318 -> policy/publish.rego:279 (deny on > 0). One rule (does a caption line fit), two implementations: DataRace text fit already used the real OFL advance table (packages/viz/src/text.ts measureText, DESIGN.md §6.2); captions did not. Technique: media-generation/platform-format-adaptation format-as-measured-template ('unmeasured is not pass': a rule with no measurement behind it must never become a validator); sound-off-first-design (captions are typography with a layout contract). Fixed: estimateLineWidth = measureText(line, fontSize, 'ui', 0, CAPTION_WEIGHT); CAPTION_WEIGHT (700) is shared with BurnedCaptions' fontWeight. Handed over from the Viz Primitives round (.claude/scan-history/findings/viz-primitives.jsonl, Lane B out-of-scope there).

## Flow
- a narrated cue line 'MERCEDES WINS AGAIN' -> estimateLineWidth 809 px <= 837 -> 0 violations
- BurnedCaptions renders it nowrap at 76 px Inter Bold -> 914 px, past the plate and the safe zone
- fix: captions depends on @statreel/viz (workspace link, lockfile regenerated) and measures with its table at the burn-in weight

## Expected impact
The publish gate now denies a render whose burned captions leave the safe zone instead of passing it. Mixed-case narration is unaffected (all recorded lines fit). Could break: a render that passed before with upper-case overflow now gets an honest deny (b6d9b28 removes the cause in segmentation).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the safe-zone count reflects real rendered width
Before: upper-cased recorded corpus (14 e2e TTS scenes, both formats): 25 of 124 cues overflow under real metrics, estimate reports 0; 'MAXIMUM WORLD TITLE' est 809 px vs real 935 px
After: same corpus: check reports 25 = real 25; mixed-case corpus 0/0 with cue signature unchanged (f93b15561e1c)
Method: gate - burned.test case seeded red on the estimate (808.64 not > 837), green on measureText; corpus run through a scratch harness
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
packages/captions/src/geometry.ts:52-53 (now measureText ... CAPTION_WEIGHT)
packages/viz/src/text.ts:85 measureText
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:318 safe_zone_violations: captionSafeZoneViolations(cues, props.format)
policy/publish.rego:279 deny when checks.safe_zone_violations > 0
probe: "MAXIMUM WORLD TITLE" est 809 real 935 inner 837; "MERCEDES WINS AGAIN" est 809 real 914
experiment (upper-cased corpus): est 0 / real 25 of 124 -> est 25 / real 25
instrument: burned.test.tsx 'measures lines with real Inter Bold advances...' (seeded red)

title: Segment cues by measured line width, not only a character count
body:
## Summary
buildCues/layoutLines broke lines by character count alone, so after the safe-zone check became honest it still produced lines the check counts (upper-case text overflowing the box).

## Description
packages/captions/src/cues.ts:76 layoutLines accepted any line with `length <= maxChars` (19 vertical / 42 landscape); width never entered segmentation. Same rule as finding 1, second implementation. Fixed: layoutLines takes an optional width predicate; buildCues passes the measured inner box (cues.ts:134). The char cap stays. A one-atom line is exempt from the width test so an unbreakable word gets a line of its own rather than a cue of its own (isolating it raised its CPS to 22.8 in the first attempt); the check still counts it. An explicit maxCharsPerLine is a cap, never a licence to leave the box. DESIGN.md §6.5 updated (it presented the 0.56 em average as the measured fit).

## Flow
- upper-case narration -> layoutLines accepts 'TITLES FOR MERCEDES' (19 chars) -> rendered 900+ px > 837
- fix: ok(line) = chars <= cap AND (single atom OR measured width <= box)

## Expected impact
Upper-case or wide-glyph narration stays on the plate; the publish gate no longer denies renders for a defect segmentation can avoid. buildCues cost 18 -> 32 ms per full 397-word narration (once per produce). Could break: segmentation of upper-case text changes (more, shorter cues).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - burned lines inside the caption box
Before: upper-cased corpus: 25 of 124 cues overflow; max CPS 17.9
After: 1 of 131 (the unbreakable 'FORTY-THIRD-HIGHEST', wider than the box alone, on its own line and still counted); max CPS 18.11 (<= 20). Mixed-case corpus: identical cue signature, 124 cues, max CPS 17.9
Method: gate - burned.test upper-case buildCues case seeded red (1 violation) then 0; cues.test layoutLines predicate case; corpus experiment both sides
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/captions/src/cues.ts:76-90 layoutLines(parts, maxChars, fits)
packages/captions/src/cues.ts:134 fitsBox = estimateLineWidth(line) <= captionTextWidth
DESIGN.md:338 cue-rule line
experiment: real 25/124 -> 1/131; maxCps 17.9 -> 18.11; mixed-case sig f93b15561e1c both sides
instrument: burned.test.tsx 'segmentation breaks by measured width too' + scratch corpus harness

title: Blank display tokens double spaces in cue lines, sidecars and burn-in
body:
## Summary
A script token with an empty display form (allowed by TokenSchema) was joined as a word: cue lines, SRT/VTT and the burn-in carried doubled spaces and a line could start with spaces.

## Description
packages/schemas/src/index.ts TokenSchema `display: z.string()` has no min. packages/captions/src/text.ts joinDisplay joined '' as a part and isGlued('') was false, so toAtoms made it an atom of its own and BurnedCaptions put a separator before it. Fixed in text.ts only: isGlued is true for a blank display and joinDisplay drops blank parts, so a blank token rides on the previous atom with no text and no separator.

## Flow
- words Fangio / '' / won / ' ' / again. -> buildCues -> lines ['Fangio  won', '  again.']
- burn-in of Fangio / '' / won -> 'Fangio  won'

## Expected impact
Captions never show a doubled space or a leading-space line for a spoken-not-shown token. Recorded corpus unchanged. Could break: nothing that shows text (joinDisplay is unchanged for non-blank parts).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - cue text equals the display text
Before: ['Fangio  won', '  again.'] and burn-in 'Fangio  won'
After: ['Fangio won again.'], burn-in 'Fangio won' with the highlight intact; corpus signature unchanged
Method: gate - two tests seeded red on the old text.ts, green on the new
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/captions/src/text.ts:7-17
packages/schemas/src/index.ts:186 display: z.string()
probe output: [[0,6.4,["Fangio  won  Next"]]]

title: Burn-in paints an empty plate for a cue the sidecars drop
body:
## Summary
BurnedCaptions drew the translucent sheet plate for a cue whose lines are all blank; toSrt/toVtt drop the same cue.

## Description
packages/captions/src/writers.ts withText drops cues with no text after cleaning; packages/captions/src/BurnedCaptions.tsx:46 only returned null for no active cue, so an all-blank cue produced an empty box over the picture for its duration. Reachable through a blank-only scene (finding 3) or a hand-built cue. Fixed: return null when every line is blank.

## Flow
- cue lines [' '] active at t -> BurnedCaptions returns the plate div with no text
- fix: `if (!cue || cue.lines.every((l) => l.trim() === '')) return null`

## Expected impact
No empty sheet flashes over the chart. Could break: nothing (a blank cue has nothing to show).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - burn-in and sidecar agree on which cues exist
Before: plate element rendered for lines [' '] and ['', '']
After: null for both
Method: gate - burned.test case seeded red, green after
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: burned.test.tsx 'paints no plate for a cue with no visible text'

title: Words-less burn-in branch untested; repeated lines share one React key
body:
## Summary
The BurnedCaptions fallback (cues without word timings - the annotation-cue shape) had no test and keyed lines by their text, so a cue repeating a line gave two siblings one key.

## Description
packages/captions/src/BurnedCaptions.tsx:97-98 `cue.lines.map((line) => <div key={line}>`; burned.test.tsx only exercised word-timed cues. Fixed: slot keys ('top'/'bottom'; CueSchema caps a cue at two lines) and a test for the branch.

## Flow
- cue {lines: ['Lap 44', 'Lap 44'], words: []} -> two divs keyed 'Lap 44'

## Expected impact
No duplicate-key reconciliation on repeated lines; the annotation path has a regression test before it is wired. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every branch of the burn-in has a test; keys unique
Before: 0 tests reach the branch; 1 key for 2 lines
After: 1 test; 2 keys for 2 lines
Method: gate - new case seeded red (1 != 2), green after
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Three source comments assert behaviour the code does not have
body:
## Summary
geometry.ts said the burn-in is white, annotations.ts said buildCues never runs, and align.ts' doc for wordsFromAlignment sat on the wrong function.

## Description
packages/captions/src/geometry.ts:5 'Inter bold, white on the ... plate' - ADR 009 made it graphite ink (videoTheme.captionInk) on a light plate. packages/captions/src/annotations.ts:4-6 'buildCues ... never runs' - apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:210 runs it on every narrated M1 produce. packages/captions/src/align.ts:15-35 two stacked JSDoc blocks (fixed: the block now sits at :29 above wordsFromAlignment): the exported function had none, the helper carried its doc. Fixed all three; no code changed.

## Flow
- developer reads annotations.ts -> treats buildCues as dead -> edits it without checking the server path

## Expected impact
Developer-facing copy matches the code. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - comments true to the code
Before: 3 claims contradicted by the code
After: 0
Method: probe - each claim read against videoTheme, pipeline.ts:210 and the JSDoc attachment; no gate can see a comment

title: Let measured width, not the 19-char proxy, cap vertical caption lines
body:
## Summary
Now that segmentation measures width, the 19-char vertical cap (a 0.56 em proxy for that width) rejects mixed-case lines that fit, producing more and shorter cues than the box needs.

## Description
packages/captions/src/cues.ts:33 maxCharsPerLine = min(32, fitCharsPerLine) = 19 vertical. 'Lewis Hamilton leads' (20 chars) measures 786 px, inside the 837 px box, yet is refused. DESIGN.md §6.5 says vertical is limited by the safe-zone width, not a char count; with width measured the proxy is redundant. Change: vertical cap -> CUE_RULES.lineLimit (32), width decides. It changes the live narrated path's segmentation and the DESIGN cue rule, so it needs its own isolated gate run (e2e replay max_cps) before landing.

## Flow
- recorded corpus vertical -> lines capped at 19 chars although ~21 fit
- B: maxCharsPerLine vertical = 32, fitsBox decides

## Expected impact
Fewer caption flips and lower reading speed on vertical. Could break: e2e replay fixtures that pin cue counts (none found; m1.spec asserts max_cps <= 20 only).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - fewer cues, lower CPS, same box
Before: recorded corpus (both formats): 124 cues, max CPS 17.9, 0 overflow
After: with the vertical cap at 32: 110 cues, max CPS 17.21, 0 overflow; upper-cased corpus unchanged (width binds)
Method: experiment - same 14 recorded scenes through buildCues on both arms in a scratch harness; not gate because the change alters a DESIGN parameter and the narrated e2e replay should run on it
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/captions/src/cues.ts:33-34
DESIGN.md:338
experiment: cues 124 -> 110, maxCps 17.9 -> 17.21, overflow 0 -> 0
instrument: scratch corpus harness over e2e/fixtures/audio alignments (cue count, max CPS, real-width overflow) + pnpm e2e replay max_cps

title: Lines and cues end on the first word of the next sentence
body:
## Summary
Segmentation leaves the first word of a new sentence dangling at the end of a line or cue ('drops. Lewis', 'the raw list. Lewis') in 8 of 236 recorded lines.

## Description
packages/captions/src/cues.ts:76-98 layoutLines rewards breaking after punctuation by only 3 against a balance score, and breakPenalty (cues.ts:104) charges 1.5 for a cue ending mid-sentence, so balance and CPS outvote the sentence boundary. Netflix/BBC line treatment avoids ending a line with the start of a new sentence. Change: penalise a line/cue whose last word follows sentence-end punctuation in the same line; guard max CPS <= 20 and cue count.

## Flow
- recorded scene 'The raw top drops. Lewis Hamilton goes from first...' -> vertical cue ['The raw top', 'drops. Lewis']
- B: add a dangling-sentence-start penalty, re-run the corpus

## Expected impact
Captions read in sentence units on the narrated path. Could break: CPS rises if cues must end at sentence edges.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - captions break at sentence boundaries
Before: 8 of 236 lines (recorded corpus, both formats) end with a sentence-start word
After: predicted 0-2 with max CPS still <= 20
Method: simulation - counted on the real corpus (A); B not built: a cost-weight change needs both arms run against the same counter
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: orphan counter /[.!?][")\]]* \S+$/ over buildCues lines of the 14 recorded scenes, with max CPS and cue count as guards

title: A cue can span a long silence and show words seconds before they are spoken
body:
## Summary
buildCues has no cost for a pause inside a cue, so words after a multi-second silence join the earlier cue and appear early.

## Description
packages/captions/src/cues.ts:164 cost = 1 + breakPenalty + cpsPenalty + short-cue penalty; nothing measures the gap between consecutive atoms. Probe: 'Fangio won' (0-0.9 s) + 'Next' at 5.9 s -> one cue [0, 6.3] 'Fangio won Next' (Next shown 5.9 s early); 'five titles.' at 4 s joins 'Fangio won' at 0. The recorded TTS corpus has no in-scene pause > 1 s (0 of 124 cues), because scenes are separate TTS calls and scene changes always break, so impact is low today.

## Flow
- words with a 5 s pause inside one scene -> one cue spanning it

## Expected impact
Captions stay in sync with speech across pauses (WCAG 1.2.2 synchronised captions). Could break: more cues on paused narration.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no word shown long before it is spoken
Before: probe: 5.9 s anticipation; recorded corpus 0 cues spanning a > 1 s pause
After: predicted <= the chosen pause threshold
Method: simulation - synthetic probe plus real-corpus count; B not built (threshold is a design parameter)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/captions/src/cues.ts:164
probe: pause 5 -> [[0,6.3,["Fangio won Next"]]]; [[0,4.8,["Fangio won","five titles."]]]
instrument: max (word.start - cue.start) for words after an in-cue gap > X s, over the property generator and the recorded corpus

title: Safe-zone deny names a count, never the line that overflowed
body:
## Summary
captionSafeZoneViolations returns only a number; the manifest and the publish deny say 'safe-zone violations' with no cue time or text, so the operator cannot find the offending caption.

## Description
packages/captions/src/geometry.ts:63 returns a count; apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:318 stores it as checks.safe_zone_violations; policy/publish.rego:278 denies with the fixed string 'safe-zone violations'. Now that the check measures honestly (964f7ac) it will fire on real renders. Change: export the offending cues (start, line, measured px) from captions and record them in the manifest; the server and policy are other contexts.

## Flow
- render with an overflowing line -> deny 'safe-zone violations' -> operator scrubs the whole video to find it

## Expected impact
A deny becomes actionable. Could break: manifest schema consumers (ProvenanceManifest checks).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failure leaves the evidence that explains it
Before: 0 of 1 deny paths name the offending cue
After: 1 of 1
Method: simulation - the seam is in apps/server and policy (out of scope for this round)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
instrument: pipeline test: a cue with an overflowing line yields a manifest entry naming its start_s and text (out-of-scope: apps/server, packages/schemas manifest)

title: Start-bump cascade can start a cue after its first word and outrun endLimit
body:
## Summary
When aligner bursts cram words into a frame or two, timeSegments pushes later cues' starts forward; a cue can then start after its first word and the last cue can end past endLimit_s.

## Description
packages/captions/src/cues.ts:212 `next.startF = endF + gapF` shifts starts; cues.ts:206 lets the last cue run to max(endLimit, natEnd) from a shifted start. 3000-seed sweep with endLimit_s = last word end: 296 cues start > 1 frame after their first word (worst 0.244 s) and 9 runs end past endLimit (worst 0.147 s). The recorded TTS corpus shows 0 late cues, so this is aligner-burst-only today.

## Flow
- burst of words in 2 frames near the end -> cue starts bumped -> last cue ends after the timeline

## Expected impact
A late-starting cue never highlights its first word; a cue past the video end lands in the sidecar. Could break: the 2-frame gap if starts are not bumped.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - cues start no later than their first word, end inside the timeline
Before: 296 late cues / 9 overruns in 3000 seeds; 0 in the recorded corpus
After: predicted 0 / 0
Method: simulation - seeded sweep measured A only; B (trim the previous cue instead of bumping) not built
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/captions/src/cues.ts:206,212
sweep: { n: 3000, cuesPastEndLimit: 9, worstPast_s: 0.147, cuesStartingAfterTheirFirstWord: 296, worstLate_s: 0.244 }
instrument: extend cues.property.test.ts: assert cue.start <= first word start + 1 frame and last end <= max(endLimit, last word end) + 1 frame

title: Vertical caption bottom hard-codes 1250 while landscape derives from the token
body:
## Summary
CAPTION_STYLE.vertical.bottom is the literal 1250; landscape computes its bottom from safeZoneLandscape.

## Description
packages/captions/src/geometry.ts:7 bottom: 1250; safeZoneVertical (packages/design-tokens/src/index.ts:68) gives 1920 - 670 = 1250. The two agree today; deriving it changes no pixel.

## Flow
- read both formats' bottom against the tokens

## Expected impact
None today; only a future token change would diverge.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for the caption bottom
Before: caption bottom 1250 px (vertical), 990 px (landscape)
After: 1250 px, 990 px - identical
Method: probe - computed both sides from the tokens
Result: not-better
Gate: none

title: Annotation cue gap repeats the literal 2 instead of CUE_RULES.minGapFrames
body:
## Summary
cuesFromAnnotations defaults gapFrames to the literal 2 while buildCues reads CUE_RULES.minGapFrames (2).

## Description
packages/captions/src/annotations.ts:47 `opts.gapFrames ?? 2`; packages/captions/src/cues.ts:13 minGapFrames: 2. Same value; swapping the literal for the constant changes no output.

## Flow
- compare both defaults

## Expected impact
None today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one constant for the Netflix gap
Before: gap 2 frames on both paths
After: 2 frames on both paths
Method: probe - read both defaults
Result: not-better
Gate: none
